messages:
Maya: @channel seeing a spike in 5xx on /v1/generate in us-west1. Error rate ~18% since 09:12 UTC. Charts in the incident dashboard look sharp. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered — paged Jen (oncall) for incident INC-2026-0934 — https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-0934
Jen (oncall): on it. grabbing logs + enabling debug sampling. will triage traces and check recent deploys. ETA 5m
Maya: pasted tail of the worker logs (snip):
```
2026-03-15T09:11:52Z worker-12 ERROR kv_cache evict failed: OOM
2026-03-15T09:12:01Z worker-08 WARN serve request slow: 1203ms
2026-03-15T09:12:07Z nginx 502 upstream prematurely closed connection
```
Liam: i'm seeing elevated p99s across the gen path too — looks correlated w/ redis/kv errors and a rolling deploy at 09:05. rolling-deploy ID: rd-778.
ops-bot: Deploy watch detected rd-778 completed at 09:05 UTC to inference-pool-us-west1. No automatic rollbacks.
Jen (oncall): ok focusing scope -> inference pool + kv cache layer. First mitigation: increase cache retention and throttle batch size to reduce pressure. Applying now.
Alice: Support note — please hold off on customer blurbs until we have a short initial update. I'll draft a concise status message we can publish.
Maya: thanks, Jen. tagging @Support-Leads to prep outbound if we need to notify high-tier customers.
Support-Leads: standing by. prep checklist: 1) initial statuspage entry, 2) org-wide internal note, 3) targeted customer e-mail if we escalate.
Jen (oncall): Draft status update (initial) — please review/edit: 
```
Status: Investigating
Component: Text Generation API (us-west1)
Impact: Some customers may experience increased errors (HTTP 5xx) and elevated latency for text generation requests in the us-west1 region.
Start time: 2026-03-15 09:12 UTC
Current status: Engineers actively investigating. We are collecting diagnostics and applying mitigations (increasing cache size, adjusting batching).
Next update: in ~30 minutes or when we have material changes.
Customer guidance: If you experience errors, retry with exponential backoff. No action required from most customers.
```
Liam: looks good. Can we remove the specific mitigation text from public copy? maybe say "mitigations in progress" instead to avoid ops detail.
Jen (oncall): good point. revised line -> "Engineers are applying mitigations to restore normal service."
Maya: +1. Add note to internal copy saying "do not mention rd-778 deploy until cause confirmed".
Alice: edited customer-facing copy below — please ack: 
```
Status: Investigating
Component: Text Generation API (us-west1)
Impact: Some customers may experience increased errors (HTTP 5xx) and elevated latency for text generation requests in the us-west1 region.
Started: 2026-03-15 09:12 UTC
What we're doing: Engineers are investigating and applying mitigations to restore normal service.
Next update: We will provide another update within 30 minutes or sooner if we have new information.
Customer guidance: If you see errors, please retry with exponential backoff and contact support if you continue to experience issues.
```
Support-Leads: approved for publish. tagging Legal for any compliance wording? not necessary yet.
Jen (oncall): publishing initial status page now (internal note first). publish command: `/status publish initial inc-2026-0934 --body "see thread"`
ops-bot: Status page entry created (draft) — https://status.redwood/incident/inc-2026-0934/draft
Maya: quick internal note for engineers: don't share dumps externally.
-- 09:30 UTC update --
Jen (oncall): Update: we've narrowed scope to KV/cache layer evictions causing cascading pressure on inference workers. Mitigation applied: increased cache retention and temporarily scaled inference pool + disabled a recent batching optimization. Error rate dropped from 18% -> ~6% in the last 10m.
Alice: updating statuspage copy for a follow-up: 
```
Update: Engineers have identified increased KV cache evictions as the likely cause. Mitigations (cache tuning + temporary scaling) are in progress and have reduced the error rate. We continue to monitor.
Next update: in 15 minutes or when more info is available.
```
Liam: telemetry shows steady decline, but p95 still elevated. keeping an eye on regressions.
Support-Leads: prepping targeted email for customers with SLO alerts. Draft snippet: "We're actively mitigating elevated errors in us-west1; our team is prioritizing customers with SLO breaches and will follow up individually."
Jen (oncall): agreed. Please hold targeted sends until we confirm stable recovery or escalate.
-- 09:52 UTC update --
Jen (oncall): Update: error rate now ~1.2%. We believe the immediate pressure is mitigated. Root cause appears to be interplay between the rd-778 deploy's batching heuristics and cache warmup, which caused eviction storms under certain traffic patterns. We're rolling back the batching change in canary and will coordinate a safer re-roll after postmortem.
Alice: prepping resolved copy once Jen signals service restored. Support-Leads: ready to send targeted notifications if we hit customers in SLO.
Maya: quick note: capture query samples and add to the incident artifact bundle for the postmortem.
-- 10:05 UTC (resolve) --
Jen (oncall): Resolved: All services restored to normal. Error rates and latency back to baseline. Root cause: batching heuristic + cache warmup interaction after rd-778 deploy. Remediation: rolled back batching change to stable variant and increased cache retention. Incident closed at 2026-03-15 10:05 UTC. Postmortem TBD.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0934 marked Resolved by Jen (oncall) at 2026-03-15 10:05 UTC.
Alice: Published final status page notice. Copy used for resolved notice: 
```
Status: Resolved
Affected component: Text Generation API (us-west1)
Impact: Intermittent 5xx errors and elevated latency were experienced by some customers between 2026-03-15 09:12 UTC and 10:05 UTC.
Resolution: The issue was caused by an interaction between a recent batching change and KV cache warmup, which led to cache evictions and increased errors. We rolled back the change and increased cache retention; service is restored.
Follow-up: A postmortem will be published with timeline and remediation actions next week.
```
Support-Leads: final outbound queued for customers with SLO impact. cc: legal, sales-eng for high-touch accounts.
Maya: thanks everyone — switching incident to postmortem channel to collect artifacts.
Jen (oncall): adding timeline + logs to INC-2026-0934 and will schedule the postmortem.
Alice: closing internal thread. Great coordination. :thumbsup:
